html:
SMTO-SKL-0100 — Your Microsoft 365 account needs to be connected again

GUID: d0b00dda-9045-5eed-ab55-d432d2f7232e
Slug: microsoft365-reauthorization-required
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • SMTO's permission to use your Microsoft account has run out, was removed, or the sign-in didn't finish. Until you sign in again, SMTO can't read or change anything in that account.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the Agent to reconnect your Microsoft 365 account, and name the account if you have more than one. Reconnecting the same account keeps its saved name and the permissions it already had.
  2. Open the sign-in link the Agent gives you within ten minutes, and sign in with the same Microsoft account as before. SMTO won't let a different Microsoft account take over this connection.
  3. After it connects, ask the Agent to do your original request again. If that request changed something, check Outlook or OneDrive first. Once permission is back, it's safe to repeat the request.

What success looks like

  • The browser page says your account is connected, and the Agent can carry out your request.

If it still fails

  • If Microsoft blocks the sign-in or asks for administrator approval, contact your Microsoft administrator. Otherwise select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The saved Microsoft 365 account cannot authorize Graph requests: its authorization_state is not available (disconnected or marked revoked), it has no refresh token, the token endpoint revoked the refresh grant, or a consent callback arrived without an authorization code.

What this means

  • Saved authorization is unavailable, refresh authorization is rejected/revoked, or browser lifecycle reports not_authorized. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Saved authorization is unavailable, refresh authorization is rejected/revoked, or browser lifecycle reports not_authorized.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect saved state and the specific refresh/browser rejection.

How to fix it

  • Call microsoft365.connect with the same auth_app_ref and account_key (the existing account_ref) so consent replaces the missing, expired or revoked refresh token for the same tenant and user. Check Entra for revoked sessions, password resets or Conditional Access changes if reauthorization recurs.
  • Reconnect the same Microsoft account using microsoft365.connect. The stored refresh authorization is missing, expired or revoked.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • A fresh supported connection restores authorization for the same intended identity.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
